items.title: noyb win: French electronics retailer Fnac Darty fined €7 million
items.description: Online & Mobile tracking Today, the French data protection authority has fined Fnac Darty (one of the largest electronics retailers in France) €7 million for illegally using third-party trackers on its mobile app without consent. The fine is the result of a noyb complaint filed in 2023. In addition to France, Fnac Darty is also active in countries such as Spain, Italy, Portugal, Belgium, and Switzerland. Press release by the French data protection authority Decision by the French data protection authority The original noyb complaints from 2023 Background. In September 2023, noyb filed three complaints in France against the real estate app SeLoger , the fitness app MyFitnessPal and the electronics retail chain Fnac Darty . The reason: The companies’ apps illegally accessed and shared users’ personal data with third parties for sophisticated analytics as soon as the apps were opened. Users

items.title: AI training platform Outlier illegally surveils European platform workers
items.description: Online & Mobile tracking Today, noyb (in collaboration with Intérêt à Agir , DIPLab and Reversing.Works ) has filed 5 complaints against Scale AI in France, Italy, the Netherlands and Austria. The US-based company operates an AI training platform named Outlier, which employs more than 900,000 “freelance” workers. Among its customers: Meta, OpenAI, Google – and the US government. However, it's not just the workers' extensive knowledge and experience that Scale AI is farming: The company collects huge amounts of personal data and forces workers to go through an invasive biometric verification to earn money. In Europe, this far-reaching workplace surveillance clearly violates the workers’ fundamental right to data protection.
